questions.q: Who introduced the AI Labeling Act?
questions.answer: Senators Brian Schatz and John Kennedy introduced the AI Labeling Act.

questions.q: What does the AI Labeling Act require?
questions.answer: The AI Labeling Act requires generative AI system developers to clearly and conspicuously disclose AI-generated content to users, take reasonable steps to prevent systematic publication of content without disclosures, and establish a working group to create non-binding technical standards.

triples.o: generative AI system developers to clearly and conspicuously disclose AI-generated content to users
developers and licensees to take reasonable steps to prevent systematic publication of content without disclosures
working group to create non-binding technical standards

questions.q: What did Senator Schatz say about the bill?
questions.answer: Senator Schatz said the bill is simple, that AI content should be labeled to prevent people from being fooled or scammed, and that it puts the onus on companies, not consumers, and helps build trust.

triples.o: Our bill is simple. If any content is made by artificial intelligence, it should be labeled so that people are aware and aren’t fooled or scammed.
It puts the onus where it belongs: on the companies and not the consumers. Labels will help people to be informed. They will also help companies using AI to build trust in their content.

questions.q: What is the Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act of 2023?
questions.answer: The Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act of 2023 (S. 3050) is a bill that proposes AI bug bounty programs, requires a vulnerability analysis study for AI-enabled military applications, and would launch reports on AI regulation in financial services and on data sharing and coordination.

second report on data sharing and coordination
